1 Enoch (Ethiopic Enoch)

Wheel of Heaven Translation

Ships A+B: Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36) + Astronomical Book (1 Enoch 72-82) — 47 chapters / 403 verses across two compositions

Direct Direct Established or uncontested across mainstream sources, or a direct description of the project itself. Framework Framework Foundational premise of the Wheel of Heaven framework. Explicit in the Raëlian canon; not endorsed by mainstream scholarship. Inferred Inferred A reasonable reading of comparative material — not stated literally, but consistent with the source. Speculative Speculative Interpretive synthesis or hypothesis that goes beyond what any single source states.

An English translation of 1 Enoch chapters 1-36 — the Book of the Watchers — produced from a per-verse layered witness reconstruction: Aramaic Dead Sea Scrolls fragments (4Q201/4Q202/4Q204/4Q205/4Q206/4Q207; the OLDEST surviving Enoch material, late 3rd c. BCE through 1st c. BCE) as the primary witness where preserved; Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus codex (6th c. CE; chs 1-32 substantially complete) as the secondary witness; Ge'ez (Ethiopic) as the tertiary witness and fallback for what neither Aramaic nor Greek preserves. The Ge'ez is the only complete witness to 1 Enoch but is the most-removed-in-time and -language from the original Aramaic composition. The Raëlian canon (per Yes... I am Raelian commentary) names 1 Enoch among the texts 'closer to the truth' — alongside the Mahābhārata, Kojiki, Popol Vuh, and the Epic of Gilgamesh. The Watchers myth (chs 6-11) — the 200 fallen angelic 'Watchers' descending to take human wives + Asael (later Azazel) teaching humanity metallurgy, weapons-craft, cosmetics, magic, and astronomical-divination — is the canon's central interest. The text expands Genesis 6:1-4 (the bnei elohim + Nephilim notice) into a fully-developed mythological narrative. Ship A scope: 36 chapters / Book of the Watchers. Ship B (chs 72-82 Astronomical Book) follows as a separate ship — the Aramaic DSS Astronomical Book (4Q208-4Q212; late 3rd c. BCE — the OLDEST Enoch fragments overall) is significantly longer than the Ge'ez recension, with much astronomical detail abbreviated in the Ge'ez transmission. The text was canonical in the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church (where it remains in the canon today) and the Beta Israel (Ethiopian Jewish) tradition. It is quoted explicitly in the New Testament (Jude 14-15 quotes 1 Enoch 1:9 + Jude 6 + 2 Peter 2:4 allude to the Watchers narrative) and was widely cited by 2nd-c. Church Fathers (Tertullian, Athenagoras, Justin Martyr) before falling out of Western and Eastern Orthodox + Roman Catholic canons in the 4th c. CE. Cross-corpus density: extremely high. Cross-corpus to Genesis 6:1-4 bnei elohim; Jude 14-15 + Jude 6 + 2 Peter 2:4 (NT citations); Shi'ur Qomah + Hekhalot Rabbati throne-vision tradition; Ezekiel 1 + Daniel 7 + Revelation 4 throne-vision chain; the Watchers tradition in Jubilees + the Testament of Reuben + Origen + Augustine; the apkallū / Seven Sages Mesopotamian antediluvian-sages tradition (cross-corpus to Adapa + Gilgamesh XI L308).

Notes Verse 2

The Aramaic ʿīrīn wĕ-qaddīšīn 'Watchers and Holy Ones' is the technical class-pairing of the angelological framework — see central entry watchers-1-enoch-6-11-bnei-elohim-cross-corpus. The Watchers' first appearance in the Aramaic Enoch corpus parallels Dan 4:13, 17, 23 (the only HB Aramaic ʿīr attestation). The WoH preserves 'Watchers' rather than collapsing to 'angels' (see overlay entry watchers-english-rendering-convention).

Notes Verse 3

ho hagios mou ho megas 'the Holy Great One' is the apophatic-divine-circumlocution title characteristic of 1 Enoch's apocalyptic register. The title is paired with hē megalē doxa 'the Great Glory' at 1 En 14:20 as the corpus's two principal divine-paraphrastic titles. See overlay entry holy-great-one-great-glory-divine-circumlocution-titles-convention.

The Sinai-theophany echo (epi to Sina oros) directly draws on Deut 33:2 + Hab 3:3 + Mic 1:3 + Ex 19. The integration of the cosmic-mountain Sinai-tradition into the 1 Enoch eschatological-judgement framework places the chapter within the broader Northwest-Semitic cosmic-mountain cluster — bidirectional with central entries har-sinai-horev-the-mountain-of-Elohim-divine-mountain-cross-corpus and mountain-as-revelation-site-mt-cross-corpus-har-sinai-mount-sapunu.

Notes Verse 9

THE JUDE 14-15 QUOTE SITE — the only OT-pseudepigraphical verse explicitly named-and-quoted as prophecy in the NT. The Aramaic ʾārū ʾāteh 'behold he comes' is preserved in the prophetic-perfect aspect; Jude 14 reads the aorist ēlthen 'he came' (a tense-shift extensively discussed in scholarship — see Bauckham 1983 WBC 93-96) and adds the explicit kyrios 'the Lord' as subject. The text-critical site is foundational; the WoH preserves the source-tense per the layered-witness convention. See central entry jude-14-15-quote-1-enoch-1-9-nt-citation-cross-corpus for the full treatment of the citation-chain Deut 33:2 → 1 En 1:9 → Dan 7:10 → Zech 14:5 → Jude 14-15 → Rev 5:11.

Notes Verse 6

Mount Hermon is the descent-site of the 200 Watchers (modern Jabal aš-Šayḫ, 2814m, on the modern Lebanese-Syrian-Israeli tri-border region — the dominant peak of the southern Levant, visible from Galilee and the Bashan plateau). The site is geographically distinct from the cosmographic seven-mountains-cluster of 1 En 18 + 24-25 (the throne-of-glory mountains in the cosmic-tour); Hermon is the terrestrial cosmic-mountain where the angelic-realm meets the human-realm. Etymological play: the Aramaic root ḥrm 'to devote/ban/oath' may underlie both the place-name and the Watchers' oath-of-mutual-binding to descend together (1 En 6:4-5). Named scholarship: Nickelsburg 2001 'Enoch, Levi, and Peter: Recipients of Revelation in Upper Galilee' JBL 100 (1981).

The Aramaic 4Q201 fragment (where reconstructable) appears to read 300 cubits; the Greek Akhmim and Ge'ez read 3000 cubits — a 10-fold textual-variant that has been extensively discussed (Milik 1976 takes 300 as original; Nickelsburg 2001 documents the dispute). The cubit-figures are theological-mythological exaggeration in the apocalyptic-narrative register, not measurements of any physical entity; popular-fringe gigantism readings are not source-textually warranted.

Notes Verse 1

THE canonical-engagement site of the 1 Enoch corpus. Asael (Aramaic ʿAśāʾēl; preserved in 4Q201/4Q202) teaches humanity metallurgy, weapons-craft (swords, knives, shields, breastplates), and cosmetics (eye-paint, ornaments, dyes). The catalog is named in the Raëlian canon per Yes... I am Raelian as a principal site reading 1 Enoch as a coded account of advanced-human-civilization technology-transfer to early humanity. The WoH translation program preserves the catalog literally and documents the acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework at the central entry asael-azazel-knowledge-transmission-1-enoch-8-canon-engagement-cross-corpus. Mainstream scholarship (Nickelsburg 2001; Reed 2005; Annus 2010) reads the catalog as the etiology-of-forbidden-knowledge within the Second-Temple-Jewish angelological framework — the materials-technology, weapons-craft, and cosmetics being the foundational categories whose introduction corrupts antediluvian humanity. Cross-corpus parallel to the Mesopotamian apkallū tradition (existing v2.56.0 adapa-apkallu-first-antediluvian-sage-paradigm-cross-corpus and v2.65.0 seven-sages-apkallu-antediluvian-knowledge-bringers-acknowledgment-cross-corpus).

The sub-list of named Watcher-instructors: Bărāqʾēl teaching astrology, Kōkabʾēl teaching constellations, Ezeqʾēl teaching cloud-knowledge, Šamšiʾēl teaching solar-knowledge, Sariʾēl teaching lunar-knowledge — the structured technical-discipline curriculum that the canonical-reception reads as a coded astronomy-and-meteorology curriculum-transfer. Each instructor's portfolio reflects the broader 1 Enoch interest in astronomical-and-calendrical knowledge (developed in the Astronomical Book, 1 En 72-82). The named-onomastics preserve the Aramaic vocalization where the Aramaic fragments witness; see overlay entry aramaic-onomastics-preservation-convention.

1

And they said one to another: ‘The earth made †without inhabitant cries the voice of their cryings† up to the gates of heaven. 3. ⌈⌈And now to you, the holy ones of heaven⌉⌉, the souls of men make their suit, saying, “Bring our cause before the Most High.”’ 4. Notes Verse 1

The Aramaic 4-archangel list (Michael, Sariel, Raphael, Gabriel) at 1 En 9:1 is the older textual-witness configuration — preserved in 4Q201/4Q202/4Q204. The expanded 7-archangel list appears at 1 En 20:1-8 in the Greek Akhmim + Ge'ez witnesses. The variant is one of the most-discussed textual-critical sites in the corpus (Milik 1976 takes the 4-list as original; Nickelsburg 2001 documents the dispute). The WoH preserves both readings per the layered-witness convention. See central entry seven-archangels-list-1-enoch-20-tob-12-rev-8-cross-corpus and overlay entry aramaic-4-vs-greek-7-archangels-textual-variant-convention.

Notes Verse 4

The binding of Asael at Dudael. Raphael is dispatched to bind Asael hand-and-foot, cast him into the wilderness opening in Dudael, cover him with darkness, place jagged-and-rough stones upon him, until the day of the great judgement when he shall be sent into the fire. The narrative is the foundational text on the Asael-as-archetypal-scapegoat-figure tradition — Reed 2005's foundational thesis that this is directly continuous with the Lev 16 Yom Kippur Azazel scapegoat tradition (the wilderness-site + stones + transfer-of-sin + eschatological-judgement framework). See central entry watchers-bound-dudael-azazel-1-enoch-10-lev-16-yom-kippur-cross-corpus. The Aramaic Dudael (Dūdāʾēl, perhaps 'the cauldron of God') and the Hebrew ʿăzāzʾēl are figures merged in transmission across the Greek and Ge'ez witnesses.

The 'seventy generations' establishes the eschatological-timeframe — the present age is the intermediate-state awaiting the cosmic-judgement.

Chapter 14

1 Enoch 14 — The throne-vision and the Great Glory

1
The book of the words of righteousness, and of the rebuke of the Watchers from of old, according to the command of the Holy Great One — in that vision which I saw.
The book of the words of righteousness, and of the reprimand of the eternal Watchers in accordance with the command of the Holy Great One in that vision. 2. I saw in my sleep what I will now say with a tongue of flesh and with the breath of my mouth: which the Great One has given to men to converse therewith and understand with the heart. 3. As He has created and given ⌈⌈to man the power of understanding the word of wisdom, so hath He created me also and given⌉⌉ me the power of reprimanding the Watchers, the children of heaven. 4. I wrote out your petition, and in my vision it appeared thus, that your petition will not be granted unto you ⌈⌈throughout all the days of eternity, and that judgement has been finally passed upon you: yea (your petition) will not be granted unto you⌉⌉. 5. And from henceforth you shall not ascend into heaven unto all eternity, and ⌈in bonds⌉ of the earth the decree has gone forth to bind you for all the days of the world. 6. And (that) previously you shall have seen the destruction of your beloved sons and ye shall have no pleasure in them, but they shall fall before you by the sword. 7. And your petition on their behalf shall not be granted, nor yet on your own: even though you weep and pray and speak all the words contained in the writing which I have written. 8. And the vision was shown to me thus: Behold, in the vision clouds invited me and a mist summoned me, and the course of the stars and the lightnings sped and hastened me, and the winds in the vision caused me to fly and lifted me upward, and bore me into heaven. 9. And I went in till I drew nigh to a wall which is built of crystals and surrounded by tongues of fire: and it began to affright me. 10. And I went into the tongues of fire and drew nigh to a large house which was built of crystals: and the walls of the house were like a tesselated floor (made) of crystals, and its groundwork was of crystal. 11. Its ceiling was like the path of the stars and the lightnings, and between them were fiery cherubim, and their heaven was (clear as) water. 12. A flaming fire surrounded the walls, and its portals blazed with fire. 13. And I entered into that house, and it was hot as fire and cold as ice: there were no delights of life therein: fear covered me, and trembling got hold upon me. 14. And as I quaked and trembled, I fell upon my face. 15. And I beheld a vision, And lo! there was a second house, greater than the former, and the entire portal stood open before me, and it was built of flames of fire. 16. And in every respect it so excelled in splendour and magnificence and extent that I cannot describe to you its splendour and its extent. 17. And its floor was of fire, and above it were lightnings and the path of the stars, and its ceiling also was flaming fire. 18. And I looked and saw ⌈⌈therein⌉⌉ a lofty throne: its appearance was as crystal, and the wheels thereof as the shining sun, and there was the vision of cherubim. 19. And from underneath the throne came streams of flaming fire so that I could not look thereon. 20. And the Great Glory sat thereon, and His raiment shone more brightly than the sun and was whiter than any snow. 21. None of the angels could enter and could behold His face by reason of the magnificence and glory and no flesh could behold Him. 22. The 1 Enoch 14 throne-vision begins — Enoch's ascent through clouds and mist and wind into the cosmic-realm. Halperin 1988 The Faces of the Chariot documents 1 En 14 as the textual fountainhead of the merkavah-mystical tradition.

Notes Verse 10

The first house of the two-house cosmography: crystal-floors, fiery walls, cherubim-decorated ceiling. The two-house architecture of 1 En 14 establishes the cosmographic-template that the Hekhalot-Merkavah tradition extends into the seven-heavens / seven-palaces (hekhalot) cosmography of Hekhalot Rabbati. Halperin 1988 documents the 1 En 14 → Hekhalot-tradition genealogy.

Notes Verse 18

The throne-of-the-Great-Glory at the heart of the second house. hē megalē doxa 'the Great Glory' is the apophatic-divine-circumlocution title characteristic of 1 Enoch — see overlay entry holy-great-one-great-glory-divine-circumlocution-titles-convention. The throne with wheels-of-shining-sun directly parallels Dan 7:9-10 (the Ancient of Days' throne-of-flames-of-fire with wheels-of-burning-fire) — the closest two parallels in all Second-Temple apocalyptic literature; the scholarly question of relative-dating and direction-of-influence between Dan 7 and 1 En 14 is genuinely contested (Nickelsburg 2001 + Collins 1993 Hermeneia Daniel).

Chapter 15

1 Enoch 15 — God's reply: the giants become evil spirits

1
And he answered me and spoke to me, and I heard his voice: Fear not, Enoch, you man of truth, scribe of truth — draw near here, and hear my voice.
And He answered and said to me, and I heard His voice: ‘Fear not, Enoch, thou righteous man and scribe of righteousness: approach hither and hear my voice. 2. And go, say to ⌈⌈the Watchers of heaven⌉⌉, who have sent thee to intercede ⌈⌈for them: "You should intercede⌉⌉ for men, and not men for you: 3. Wherefore have ye left the high, holy, and eternal heaven, and lain with women, and defiled yourselves with the daughters of men and taken to yourselves wives, and done like the children of earth, and begotten giants (as your) sons? 4. And though ye were holy, spiritual, living the eternal life, you have defiled yourselves with the blood of women, and have begotten (children) with the blood of flesh, and, as the children of men, have lusted after flesh and blood as those ⌈also⌉ do who die and perish. 5. Therefore have I given them wives also that they might impregnate them, and beget children by them, that thus nothing might be wanting to them on earth. 6. But you were ⌈formerly⌉ spiritual, living the eternal life, and immortal for all generations of the world. 7. And therefore I have not appointed wives for you; for as for the spiritual ones of the heaven, in heaven is their dwelling. 8. And now, the giants, who are produced from the spirits and flesh, shall be called evil spirits upon the earth, and on the earth shall be their dwelling. 9. Evil spirits have proceeded from their bodies; because they are born from men ⌈⌈and⌉⌉ from the holy Watchers is their beginning and primal origin; ⌈they shall be evil spirits on earth, and⌉ evil spirits shall they be called. 10. [As for the spirits of heaven, in heaven shall be their dwelling, but as for the spirits of the earth which were born upon the earth, on the earth shall be their dwelling.] 11. And the spirits of the giants afflict, oppress, destroy, attack, do battle, and work destruction on the earth, and cause trouble: they take no food, ⌈but nevertheless hunger⌉ and thirst, and cause offences. 12. And these spirits shall rise up against the children of men and against the women, because they have proceeded ⌈from them⌉.

Notes Verse 8

The foundational demonological etiology of Second-Temple Judaism and Patristic Christianity. The disembodied spirits of the dead giants become the evil-spirits / demons of the post-flood world: 'the spirits of the giants ... shall be called evil spirits upon the earth; they shall be called evil spirits; for their dwelling shall be upon the earth and within the earth; evil spirits proceeded from their bodies, because they were born from above and the beginning of their creation was from the holy Watchers' (1 En 15:8-9). The etiology supplies the framework that Jub 10, Justin Martyr 2 Apol 5, Athenagoras, and Tertullian De Idololatria 9 all develop systematically. See central entry giants-become-evil-spirits-demonology-1-enoch-15-cross-corpus-jub-10-tertullian.

Notes Verse 11

The catalog of demonic-activities: 'afflict, oppress, destroy, attack, do battle, work destruction on the earth, and cause trouble; they take no food, but nevertheless hunger and thirst, and cause offences' — the foundational Second-Temple-and-Patristic catalog of demonic-activities, supplying the framework for later Christian-monastic, Hekhalot-magical, and rabbinic demonologies.

Notes Verse 1

The Greek 7-archangel list (Uriel, Raphael, Raguel, Michael, Sariel/Saraqael, Gabriel, Remeiel) is the developed-canonical form preserved in the Greek Akhmim + Ge'ez witnesses. Each archangel has a distinct cosmic-administrative portfolio; the list is the textual fountainhead of the developed Jewish angelological tradition. Cross-corpus to Tobit 12:15 (Raphael, 'one of the seven holy angels'); Rev 8:2 (the seven angels who stand before God). The Aramaic 4-archangel list at 1 En 9:1 is the older textual-witness configuration — both are preserved per the layered-witness convention. See central entry seven-archangels-list-1-enoch-20-tob-12-rev-8-cross-corpus and overlay aramaic-4-vs-greek-7-archangels-textual-variant-convention.

1 Enoch 21 — The prison of the rebellious stars and the prison of the fallen angels

1
And I went round about as far as a place where nothing is made.
And I proceeded to where things were chaotic. 2. And I saw there something horrible: I saw neither a heaven above nor a firmly founded earth, but a place chaotic and horrible. 3. And there I saw seven stars of the heaven bound together in it, like great mountains and burning with fire. 4. Then I said: ‘For what sin are they bound, and on what account have they been cast in hither?’ 5. Then said Uriel, one of the holy angels, who was with me, and was chief over them, and said: ‘Enoch, why dost thou ask, and why art thou eager for the truth? 6. These are of the number of the stars ⌈of heaven⌉, which have transgressed the commandment of the Lord, and are bound here till ten thousand years, the time entailed by their sins, are consummated.’ 7. And from thence I went to another place, which was still more horrible than the former, and I saw a horrible thing: a great fire there which burnt and blazed, and the place was cleft as far as the abyss, being full of great descending columns of fire: neither its extent or magnitude could I see, nor could I conjecture. 8. Then I said: ‘How fearful is the place and how terrible to look upon!’ 9. Then Uriel answered me, one of the holy angels who was with me, and said unto me: ‘Enoch, why hast thou such fear and affright?’ And I answered: ‘Because of this fearful place, and because of the spectacle of the pain.’ 10. And he said ⌈⌈unto me⌉⌉: ‘This place is the prison of the angels, and here they will be imprisoned for ever.’

Notes Verse 1

Enoch's tour reaches the cosmographic-confinement-site of the stars who transgressed the commandment of the Lord. The fallen-stars framework integrates astronomical-regularity with cosmic-moral-obligation — the stars who 'failed to come forth in their appointed times' are bound as cosmic-rebels. The framework develops at length in the Astronomical Book (1 En 72-82, Ship B). See central entry fallen-stars-prison-1-enoch-18-21-jude-6-2-pet-2-4-cross-corpus.

Notes Verse 1

Enoch's tour reaches the great mountain in the West with four hollow places — the foundational Second-Temple-Jewish text on the intermediate-state of the dead. The chapter establishes the moral-typology of the dead (righteous / sinners-not-yet-judged / unjustly-killed / wicked-already-punished) and the intermediate-state between death and final judgement. See central entry four-hollow-places-of-the-dead-1-enoch-22-intermediate-state-cross-corpus. Cross-corpus to Luke 16:22-26 (Lazarus-and-the-rich-man parable's intermediate-state cosmography), Rev 6:9-10 (souls of the martyrs under the altar), 4 Ezra 7:75-101, 2 Bar 21:23-24.

The tree of life shall be transplanted to the holy place by the temple of the Lord, the Eternal King. The eschatological-restoration: the tree-of-life is reserved for the righteous at the great judgement; afterward it is transplanted to the cosmographic-center. The framework is inherited by Rev 22:2, 22:14 (the tree of life in the new Jerusalem); the Rev 22 → 1 En 25 dependency is foundational (Bauckham 1993 Climax of Prophecy 310-321).

Notes Verse 1

The accursed valley — the foundational text for the Second-Temple-Jewish and NT geenna eschatological-judgement-site tradition. The cosmography places the accursed-valley in proximity to Jerusalem (continuing the historical-geographical association with the Valley of Hinnom / Topheth precinct of Jer 7:31-32, 19:6 + 2 Kgs 23:10) while developing it into the cosmographic-eschatological-judgement-site framework. See central entry gehenna-valley-of-hinnom-1-enoch-27-nt-cross-corpus. Cross-corpus to the 12 NT geenna references (Mt 5:22, 5:29-30, 10:28, 18:9, 23:15, 23:33; Mark 9:43-47; Luke 12:5; James 3:6) and to the rabbinic gehinnōm tradition.

Notes Verse 1

Enoch's eastern-paradise tour begins — the aromatic-trees-and-spices garden (cassia, cinnamon, aloes, nard, mastic, balsam, frankincense, galbanum). The 1 En 28-32 catalog is one of the most-detailed in the Second-Temple-Jewish corpus and reflects the Hellenistic-period interest in spice-trade vocabulary. See central entry enoch-eastern-paradise-gan-eden-aromatic-trees-1-enoch-28-32-cross-corpus.

Notes Verse 3

The tree of wisdom — Raphael identifies as the Gen 3 tree of which Adam and Eve ate. The 1 En 32 'tree of wisdom' redeploys the Hebrew Bible etz ha-da'at tov va-ra 'tree of the knowing of good and bad' with the Second-Temple-Jewish Sophia / Hokhmah personification-vocabulary. The 1 En 32 framing is more nuanced than the Hebrew Bible reading: 'they learned wisdom and their eyes were opened' is quasi-positive. See central entry tree-of-wisdom-1-enoch-32-gen-3-sophia-cross-corpus. Cross-corpus to Prov 8 + Wis Sol 7-9 (the Sophia-personification tradition); to Gnostic-Christian readings (Hypostasis of the Archons; Apocryphon of John); to existing central entries etz-chayim-daat, niphqecho-eineihem, ke-elohim.

Notes Verse 1

The Astronomical Book opens with two foundational framing-moves. The opening verse of 1 En 72 establishes (i) Uriel as the principal-revealing-angel of the Astronomical Book — the malʾaku qəddus 'holy angel' who is marḥomu 'their leader' (over the luminaries); and (ii) the eschatological-horizon of the cosmographic-revelation — the 'new creation that abides forever' (fəṭrat ḥaddis zayənabbər la-ʿālam).

Uriel as cosmic-administrative-angel. The Ge'ez marḥomu ('their leader') establishes Uriel's portfolio in the Astronomical Book as the cosmic-administrative-angel over the luminaries. The role is consistent with the seven-archangel-list at 1 En 20:2 where Uriel is 'over the world and Tartarus'; the Astronomical Book Uriel is the developed-form of the cosmic-administrative-angel-figure that runs through 1 En 21:5 (Uriel as tour-guide to the place-of-judgement for fallen stars), through ch 75 + 79 + 82 (Uriel's calendrical-leadership), into the 4 Ezra Uriel-as-Ezra's-revelatory-angel tradition, and ultimately into the Hekhalot-Merkavah Sar ha-Olam 'Prince of the World' cosmic-administrative-angel-figure. See central entries uriel-angel-over-luminaries-1-enoch-72-79-82-cross-corpus and seven-archangels-list-1-enoch-20-tob-12-rev-8-cross-corpus.

The Astronomical Book as a unit. This verse opens what is — by manuscript-witness — the OLDEST stratum of the 1 Enoch corpus. The Aramaic 4Q208 + 4Q209 fragments (palaeographically dated late 3rd c. BCE per Milik 1976; Tigchelaar-García Martínez DJD XXXVI 2000) predate the Aramaic Book-of-the-Watchers fragments (4Q201/4Q202) and constitute the earliest surviving Enoch material overall. The Astronomical Book has NO Greek witness — the Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus ends mid-ch 32. See central entry astronomical-book-1-enoch-72-82-aramaic-dss-oldest-witness-unit-entry and overlay entry astronomical-book-no-greek-witness-aramaic-geez-only-convention.

The 'new creation' eschatological-horizon. The phrase fəṭrat ḥaddis 'new creation' anticipates the eschatological-cosmological renewal that becomes one of the most-persistent Second-Temple-period and downstream eschatological frameworks: Isa 65:17 (hinnĕnî bôrēʾ šāmayim ḥădāšîm wā-ʾāreṣ ḥădāšâ 'behold, I create new heavens and a new earth'), Isa 66:22 (the new-heavens-and-new-earth standing-forever), Jub 1:29 + 4:26 (the renewal of all the luminaries), 1 En 91:16 (Apocalypse-of-Weeks), and Rev 21:1 (the new heaven and the new earth). The Astronomical-Book opening positions the cosmographic-revelation as until the new creation — that is, the present-cosmic-order (which the Astronomical Book describes) is bracketed within a longer eschatological-horizon. The 'new creation' cluster spans the Second-Temple-Jewish-and-NT eschatological framework as a developed-tradition.

3
And I saw six gates through which the sun comes forth, and six gates through which the sun sets; and the moon also rises and sets in those gates, together with the leaders of the stars and those whom they lead: six in the east and six in the west, all of them ranged one after another in their order; and many side-windows are alongside them on the right and on the left of those gates.
ወርእኩ፡ wa-rəʾku ስድስቱ፡ sədəstu አናቅጸ፡ ʾanāqəḍa እምኔሆሙ፡ ʾəmənnehomu ይወፅእ፡ yəwaḍḍəʾ ፀሐይ፡ ḍaḥay ወስድስቱ፡ wa-sədəstu አናቅጸ፡ ʾanāqəḍa እምኔሆሙ፡ ʾəmənnehomu ይዐርብ፡ yəʿarrəb ፀሐይ፡ ḍaḥay ወወርኅሂ፡ wa-warḫəni ይወፅእ፡ yəwaḍḍəʾ ወይዐርብ፡ wa-yəʿarrəb በውስቴቶሙ፡ ba-wəstētomu ወመራኅያነ፡ wa-marāḫəyāna ከዋክብት፡ kawākəbt ምስለ፡ məsla መሪሖሙ፡ marihomu ስድስቱ፡ sədəstu በምሥራቅ፡ ba-məśrāq ወስድስቱ፡ wa-sədəstu በምዕራብ፡ ba-məʿrāb ኵሎሙ፡ kwəlomu በበ፡ baba ዚአሁ፡ ziʾahu ተራሕው፡ tarāḥwə ድኅረ፡ dəḫra ካልኡ፡ kāləʾu ወብዙኃንኒ፡ wa-bəzuḫāni ጠባት፡ ṭabāt በኀበ፡ ba-ḫaba ካልኦቶሙ፡ kāləʾotomu በኤምነ፡ ba-ʾēmna ወበፅግመ፡ wa-ba-ḍəgma እማንቱ፡ ʾəmāntu አናቅጽ፡ ʾanāqəḍ
4
And first there comes forth the great luminary, whose name is the sun, by the fourth of those six eastern gates.
ወቀዲሙ፡ wa-qadimu ይወፅእ፡ yəwaḍḍəʾ ብርሃኑ፡ bərhānu ለፀሐይ፡ la-ḍaḥay ዐቢይ፡ ʿabəy ዘውእቱ፡ zawəʾətu ስሙ፡ səmu በአንቀጽ፡ ba-ʾanqaḍ ራብዕ፡ rābəʿ እምነ፡ ʾəmənna ስድስቱ፡ sədəstu አናቅጽ፡ ʾanāqəḍ እማንቱ፡ ʾəmāntu ቀዳማዊያን፡ qadāmāwəyān ምሥራቃውያን፡ məśrāqāwəyān
5
And in that fourth gate from which the sun comes forth in the first month there are twelve windows opened, from which a flame issues whenever they are opened in their seasons.
ወውስተ፡ wa-wəsta ይእቲ፡ yəʾəti አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ ራብዕት፡ rābəʿt እንተ፡ ʾənta እምኔሃ፡ ʾəmənnehā ይወፅእ፡ yəwaḍḍəʾ ፀሐይ፡ ḍaḥay ቀዳማዌ፡ qadāmāwē ወርኀ፡ warḫa ሀለዉ፡ hallawu ዐሠርቱ፡ ʿaśartu ወክልኤቱ፡ wa-kəlʾētu መሣክው፡ masākəw ክሥቱት፡ kəśtut እምኔሆሙ፡ ʾəmənnehomu ይወፅእ፡ yəwaḍḍəʾ ነበልባል፡ nabalbāl ሶበ፡ soba ይትረኀዉ፡ yətrəḫḫawu በበ፡ baba ጊዜሆሙ፡ gizēhomu
6
When the sun rises in heaven, it comes forth through that fourth gate for thirty days, and sets, according to its law, in the fourth gate of the western heaven.
ወሶበ፡ wa-soba ይወፅእ፡ yəwaḍḍəʾ ፀሐይ፡ ḍaḥay በሰማይ፡ ba-samāy ይወፅእ፡ yəwaḍḍəʾ በይእቲ፡ ba-yəʾəti አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ ራብዕት፡ rābəʿt ሠላሳ፡ śallāsā መዋዕለ፡ mawāʿəla ወይዐርብ፡ wa-yəʿarrəb በከመ፡ bakama ሕገጊሁ፡ ḥəgagihu በውስተ፡ ba-wəsta አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ ራብዒት፡ rābəʿit እንተ፡ ʾənta ምዕራብ፡ məʿrāb ሰማይ፡ samāy
7
And in those days the day grows longer than the night, and the day continues to grow longer than the night until the sun's rising reaches the fourth gate. The day approaches twice the night, and the day amounts to twelve parts and the night to ten parts.
ወበእማንቱ፡ wa-ba-ʾəmāntu መዋዕል፡ mawāʿəl ይነውኅ፡ yənawwəḫ መዓልት፡ maʿālt እምነ፡ ʾəmənna ሌሊት፡ lēlit ወይትዌሰክ፡ wa-yətwēsak መዓልት፡ maʿālt እምነ፡ ʾəmənna ሌሊት፡ lēlit ዘእንበለ፡ za-ʾənbala ይብጻሕ፡ yəbṣāḥ ብርሃኑ፡ bərhānu ለፀሐይ፡ la-ḍaḥay አንቀጸ፡ ʾanqaḍa ራብዕተ፡ rābəʿta ይነዊኅ፡ yənawiḫ መዓልት፡ maʿālt ቅሩበ፡ qəruba ካዕበ፡ kāʿba ምስለ፡ məsla ሌሊት፡ lēlit ወይከውን፡ wa-yəkawwən መዓልት፡ maʿālt ዐሠርተ፡ ʿaśarta ክልኤተ፡ kəlʾēta ክፋላተ፡ kəfālāta ወሌሊት፡ wa-lēlit ይከውን፡ yəkawwən ዐሠርተ፡ ʿaśarta ክፋላተ፡ kəfālāta
Notes Verse 7

The 22-part day-ratio system begins here. The ratio 12+10 = 22 parts inaugurates one of two parallel day-ratio systems that coexist within 1 En 72 without explicit harmonization. The other system — the 18-part system at the solstice-extremes — appears at vv. 11 + 21 (12+6 = 18 parts). The dual-system situation is one of the most-discussed astronomical-textual-cruxes of the Astronomical Book; the WoH translation preserves both systems verbatim without harmonization, per the source-internal-inconsistency convention. See overlay entry 18-vs-22-part-day-ratio-scholarly-crux-1-enoch-72-7-no-harmonization-convention and the foundational scholarly treatment in O. Neugebauer The Astronomical Chapters of the Ethiopic Book of Enoch (72-82) (1981; reprinted as appendix to Black 1985).

8
And the sun comes forth from that fourth gate and sets in the fourth gate, and it returns to the fifth gate in the east for thirty days, and it comes forth from it and sets in the fifth gate.
ወይወፅእ፡ wa-yəwaḍḍəʾ ፀሐይ፡ ḍaḥay እምይእቲ፡ ʾəmyəʾəti አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ ራብዕት፡ rābəʿt ወይዐርብ፡ wa-yəʿarrəb በራብዒት፡ ba-rābəʿit ወይትገብእ፡ wa-yətgabbəʾ ኀበ፡ ḫaba ኃምስት፡ ḫāməst አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ በምሥራቅ፡ ba-məśrāq ሠላሳ፡ śallāsā መዋዕለ፡ mawāʿəla ወይወፅእ፡ wa-yəwaḍḍəʾ እምኔሃ፡ ʾəmənnehā ወይዐርብ፡ wa-yəʿarrəb በኃምስት፡ ba-ḫāməst አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ
9
And when the sun comes forth from the fifth gate for thirty days, the day grows longer, and amounts to thirteen parts, and the night to nine parts.
ወአመ፡ wa-ʾama ይወፅእ፡ yəwaḍḍəʾ ፀሐይ፡ ḍaḥay እምነ፡ ʾəmənna ኃምስት፡ ḫāməst አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ ሠላሳ፡ śallāsā መዋዕለ፡ mawāʿəla ይነውኅ፡ yənawwəḫ መዓልት፡ maʿālt ወይከውን፡ wa-yəkawwən ዐሠርተ፡ ʿaśarta ሠለስተ፡ śallasta ክፋላተ፡ kəfālāta ወሌሊት፡ wa-lēlit ዘጠዐ፡ zaṭaʿ ክፋላተ፡ kəfālāta
10
And the sun returns to the east and enters the sixth gate, and it comes forth and sets in the sixth gate for thirty-one days, on account of its sign.
ወይትገብእ፡ wa-yətgabbəʾ ፀሐይ፡ ḍaḥay ምሥራቀ፡ məśrāqa ወይበውእ፡ wa-yəbawwəʾ ውስተ፡ wəsta ሳድስ፡ sādəs አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ ወይወፅእ፡ wa-yəwaḍḍəʾ ወይዐርብ፡ wa-yəʿarrəb በሳድስ፡ ba-sādəs አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ ሠላሳ፡ śallāsā ወአሐደ፡ wa-ʾaḥada መዋዕለ፡ mawāʿəla በእንተ፡ ba-ʾənta ምልክቱ፡ məlkətu
11
And on that day the day becomes twice as long as the night, and the day amounts to twelve parts, and the night is shortened and amounts to six parts.
ወይነውኅ፡ wa-yənawwəḫ መዓልት፡ maʿālt እምነ፡ ʾəmənna ይእቲ፡ yəʾəti ሳድስ፡ sādəs አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ ካዕበ፡ kāʿba ምስለ፡ məsla ሌሊት፡ lēlit ወይከውን፡ wa-yəkawwən መዓልት፡ maʿālt ዐሠርተ፡ ʿaśarta ወክልኤተ፡ wa-kəlʾēta ክፋላተ፡ kəfālāta ወሌሊት፡ wa-lēlit የሐጽጽ፡ yaḥaḍḍəḍ ወይከውን፡ wa-yəkawwən ስድስተ፡ sədəsta ክፋላተ፡ kəfālāta
12
And the sun returns and enters the fifth gate, and it comes forth and sets in the fifth gate for thirty days.
ወይትገብእ፡ wa-yətgabbəʾ ፀሐይ፡ ḍaḥay ወይበውእ፡ wa-yəbawwəʾ ውስተ፡ wəsta ኃምስ፡ ḫāməs አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ ወይወፅእ፡ wa-yəwaḍḍəʾ ወይዐርብ፡ wa-yəʿarrəb በኃምስ፡ ba-ḫāməs አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ ሠላሳ፡ śallāsā መዋዕለ፡ mawāʿəla
13
And the day amounts to thirteen parts and the night to nine parts.
ወይነውኅ፡ wa-yənawwəḫ መዓልት፡ maʿālt ወይከውን፡ wa-yəkawwən ዐሠርተ፡ ʿaśarta ሠለስተ፡ śallasta ክፋላተ፡ kəfālāta ወሌሊት፡ wa-lēlit ዘጠዐ፡ zaṭaʿ ክፋላተ፡ kəfālāta
14
And the sun returns from the fifth gate and enters the fourth gate for thirty days; it comes forth and sets in the fourth gate.
ወይትገብእ፡ wa-yətgabbəʾ ፀሐይ፡ ḍaḥay እምነ፡ ʾəmənna ኃምስ፡ ḫāməs አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ ወይበውእ፡ wa-yəbawwəʾ ራብዐ፡ rābəʿa አንቀጸ፡ ʾanqaḍa ሠላሳ፡ śallāsā መዋዕለ፡ mawāʿəla ይወፅእ፡ yəwaḍḍəʾ ወይዐርብ፡ wa-yəʿarrəb በራብዕ፡ ba-rābəʿ አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ
15
And the day becomes equal to the night, and they encompass one another; the day amounts to eleven parts and the night to eleven parts.
ወይትዐረዩ፡ wa-yətʿarrayu መዓልት፡ maʿālt ምስለ፡ məsla ሌሊት፡ lēlit ወይትከበቡ፡ wa-yətkababu ወይከውን፡ wa-yəkawwən መዓልት፡ maʿālt ዐሠርተ፡ ʿaśarta ወአሐደ፡ wa-ʾaḥada ክፋላተ፡ kəfālāta ወሌሊት፡ wa-lēlit ይከውን፡ yəkawwən ዐሠርተ፡ ʿaśarta ወአሐደ፡ wa-ʾaḥada ክፋላተ፡ kəfālāta
16
And the sun returns and enters the third gate, and it comes forth and sets in the third gate for thirty-one days.
ወይትገብእ፡ wa-yətgabbəʾ ፀሐይ፡ ḍaḥay ወይበውእ፡ wa-yəbawwəʾ ውስተ፡ wəsta ሣልስ፡ śāləs አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ ወይወፅእ፡ wa-yəwaḍḍəʾ ወይዐርብ፡ wa-yəʿarrəb በሣልስ፡ ba-śāləs አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ ሠላሳ፡ śallāsā ወአሐደ፡ wa-ʾaḥada መዋዕለ፡ mawāʿəla
17
And the night grows longer than the day, until the third gate; the night amounts to twelve parts and the day to ten parts.
ወይነውኅ፡ wa-yənawwəḫ ሌሊት፡ lēlit እምነ፡ ʾəmənna መዓልት፡ maʿālt እስከ፡ ʾəska አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ ሣልስ፡ śāləs ወይከውን፡ wa-yəkawwən ሌሊት፡ lēlit ዐሠርተ፡ ʿaśarta ክልኤተ፡ kəlʾēta ክፋላተ፡ kəfālāta ወመዓልት፡ wa-maʿālt ይከውን፡ yəkawwən ዐሠርተ፡ ʿaśarta ክፋላተ፡ kəfālāta
18
And the sun returns from the third gate and enters the second gate in the east for thirty days.
ወይትገብእ፡ wa-yətgabbəʾ ፀሐይ፡ ḍaḥay እምነ፡ ʾəmənna ሣልስ፡ śāləs አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ ወይበውእ፡ wa-yəbawwəʾ ካልዕተ፡ kāləʿta አንቀጸ፡ ʾanqaḍa ምሥራቅ፡ məśrāq ሠላሳ፡ śallāsā መዋዕለ፡ mawāʿəla
19
And the night grows longer and amounts to thirteen parts, and the day is shortened and amounts to nine parts.
ወይነውኅ፡ wa-yənawwəḫ ሌሊት፡ lēlit ወይከውን፡ wa-yəkawwən ዐሠርተ፡ ʿaśarta ሠለስተ፡ śallasta ክፋላተ፡ kəfālāta ወመዓልት፡ wa-maʿālt የሐጽጽ፡ yaḥaḍḍəḍ ወይከውን፡ wa-yəkawwən ዘጠዐ፡ zaṭaʿ ክፋላተ፡ kəfālāta
20
And the sun returns from the second gate and enters the first gate for thirty-one days, and sets in the first gate of the west.
ወይትገብእ፡ wa-yətgabbəʾ ፀሐይ፡ ḍaḥay እምነ፡ ʾəmənna ካልዕት፡ kāləʿt አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ ወይበውእ፡ wa-yəbawwəʾ ቀዳሚተ፡ qadāmita አንቀጸ፡ ʾanqaḍa ሠላሳ፡ śallāsā ወአሐደ፡ wa-ʾaḥada መዋዕለ፡ mawāʿəla ወይዐርብ፡ wa-yəʿarrəb በቀዳሚት፡ ba-qadāmit አንቀጽ፡ ʾanqaḍ እንተ፡ ʾənta ምዕራብ፡ məʿrāb

Notes Verse 32

The 364-day-year statement — the calendrical-identity-keystone of the Astronomical Book and the broader Qumran-Enochic-Jubilees corpus. This verse is the explicit-foundational-statement of the 364-day solar calendar: the sun's annual circuit through the twelve gates of heaven completes 364 days. The mathematical-elegance of the 364-day year (52 weeks × 7 days = 364 days; four seasons × 91 days each = 364 days; festival-dates always fall on the same day of the week) is essential to the calendar's appeal and its identity-marker status. The 364-day calendar is the calendrical-identity-keystone of the Qumran community vis-à-vis the proto-Rabbinic / Pharisaic Temple-Establishment lunar-solar tradition.

Cross-corpus to Jubilees 6:32-38. The Jubilees parallel polemic at 6:32-38 makes the calendrical-identity-keystone status explicit: 'they will forget the new moons and the times and the sabbaths, and they will make mistakes in all the new months and times and sabbaths ... if they walk in the times of the Gentiles and follow their ways'. The 364-day calendar is presented in Jubilees as the divinely-ordained calendar inscribed in the heavenly-tablets; the proto-Rabbinic lunar calendar is presented as cosmic-disorder and ritual-impurity.

Cross-corpus to the Qumran calendrical texts. The Qumran community produced an extensive corpus of calendrical-implementation-texts (4Q319 Otot; 4Q320-4Q321a + 4Q325-4Q330 Mishmarot; 4Q252; 4QMMT B; 11Q5 col 27 'David's Compositions' attributing 364 psalms-per-year to David; CD 16:2-3). The 364-day calendar was a working-calendar of the Qumran community, not merely a theoretical-ideal.

The 364-day-vs-365.25-day mathematical problem. The 364-day year is short of the actual tropical year (~365.25 days) by 1.25 days per year; over time, this discrepancy accumulates. Multiple harmonization-strategies have been proposed in scholarship (Glessmer 1999; Beckwith 1996; Stern 2001); the WoH translation preserves the source-text 364-day-year without modernization. See central entry qumran-364-day-solar-calendar-polemic-1-enoch-72-82-jubilees-cross-corpus and overlay entry 364-day-solar-calendar-rendering-convention.

Notes Verse 37

The 7:1 sun:moon luminosity ratio + the corrupted-Ge'ez scribal-repetition. The verse states the 7:1 sun:moon luminosity ratio that organizes the Astronomical Book's framework of the 'greater luminary' (sun) and 'lesser luminary' (moon) — paralleling the Gen 1:14-19 meʾōrôt gĕdōlîm / qāṭān framework. The 7:1 ratio is one of the schematic-ideal-ratios characteristic of the Astronomical Book; it does not correspond to modern-astronomical measurements of solar-vs-lunar luminosity but operates within the source-text-schematic register.

The Ge'ez of v. 37 is textually difficult. The repeated phrasing 'sevenfold against the sun's light is reckoned' appears multiple times in the Ge'ez witness — Charles 1912 noted the scribal-repetition as corrupted; Knibb 1978 preserves the Ge'ez verbatim; the modern critical-editions (Nickelsburg-VanderKam 2012 Hermeneia vol 2) document the corruption without proposing definitive emendation. The WoH translation preserves the Ge'ez verbatim per the per-verse layered-witness convention.

Cross-corpus to Isa 30:26 — the eschatological sun-moon-light-reversal. Isa 30:26 wĕ-hāyâ ʾôr ha-lĕbānâ kĕ-ʾôr ha-ḥammâ wĕ-ʾôr ha-ḥammâ yihyeh šiḇʿātayim 'and the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold' — the eschatological-reversal of the natural-cosmic-order where the moon's light becomes equal to the sun's and the sun's light becomes sevenfold its present-state. The Isa 30:26 framework parallels the 1 En 72:37 7:1 ratio but inverts the present-state-ratio into the eschatological-reversal.

1 Enoch 73 — The moon's nature and her monthly waxing

1
And after this law I saw another law for the lesser luminary, whose name is the moon.
The First Parable. When the congregation of the righteous shall appear, And sinners shall be judged for their sins, And shall be driven from the face of the earth:
ወእምድኅረዝ፡ wa-ʾəmdəḫrazə ሕግ፡ ḥəg ርእኩ፡ rəʾku ሕገ፡ ḥəga ካልዕተ፡ kāləʿta ለብርሃን፡ la-bərhān ዘንዑስ፡ zanəʿus ዘስሙ፡ zasəmu ወርኅ፡ warḫ
2
And he set forth for it its whole course according to its laws, and the reckoning of its light for all its days.

It had been good for them if they had not been born.
ወሰፍሐ፡ wa-safḥa ሎቱ፡ lotu ኵሎ፡ kwəlo ሑረቶ፡ ḥurato በበ፡ baba ሕገጊሁ፡ ḥəgagihu ወብርሃኖ፡ wa-bərhāno ኆለቆ፡ ḫolaqo ለመዋዕሊሁ፡ la-mawāʿəlihu ኵሉ፡ kwəlu
3
And her light is the moon's light, which is sevenfold less than the light of the sun; and in the great reckoning the light of the sun is measured against the full light of the moon.

ወብርሃኑ፡ wa-bərhānu ሰብዐ፡ sabʿa ምስለ፡ məsla ብርሃና፡ bərhānā ለፀሐይ፡ la-ḍaḥay ይከውን፡ yəkawwən ብርሃና፡ bərhānā ለወርኅ፡ la-warḫ ወበዐቢይ፡ wa-ba-ʿabəy ኆለቅ፡ ḫolaq ይከውን፡ yəkawwən ብርሃና፡ bərhānā ለፀሐይ፡ la-ḍaḥay ይትዌቅሕ፡ yətwaḳḳəḥ ምልዕተ፡ məlʿta ብርሃና፡ bərhānā ለወርኅ፡ la-warḫ

Notes Verse 4

Aramaic-PRIMARY witness — 4Q209 frag 7 col. ii. This verse is preserved in the Aramaic 4Q209 fragment in fuller form than the Ge'ez transmission. The 14-day-waxing + full-moon-at-two-weeks is the foundational lunar-month structure of the Astronomical Book; the Aramaic 4Q208 + 4Q209 fragments preserve a much fuller day-by-day fractional tabulation (the seven-part visible-light grid divided into half-parts, giving a 49-unit-fractional grid for the synodic cycle) that the Ge'ez transmission has heavily abbreviated.

The witness-fullness-inversion at chs 73-74 (the Aramaic preserves more than the Ge'ez) is unusual within the 1 Enoch corpus and is one of the most-distinctive textual-features of the Astronomical Book. The original Aramaic Astronomical Book was substantially longer than what the Ge'ez preserves — perhaps two or three times the surviving Ge'ez length. See overlay entry aramaic-fuller-than-geez-lunar-tables-4q208-convention and the foundational scholarly treatment in H. Drawnel The Aramaic Astronomical Book (4Q208-4Q211) from Qumran (Oxford 2011).

Notes Verse 6

The 1/7 + 1/14 = 3/14 fractional formula for day 1 of the lunar month. The verse states the lunar-disk-visible-fraction for day 1 of the synodic cycle: one seventh + one fourteenth = 3/14 of the disk visible. The Ge'ez transmission of this verse is acknowledged corrupted (Charles 1912 noted the corruption; conjectures various emendations of the 1/14 × 1/7 fractional formula); the Aramaic 4Q208 stratum preserves a dramatically fuller computational-tabulation for the day-by-day fractional progression across the synodic cycle. The WoH translation preserves the Ge'ez witness verbatim per the per-verse layered-witness convention; the corrupted-state is flagged.

Notes Verse 11

The 354-vs-364 day-gap — Aramaic-PRIMARY witness. This verse explicitly states the 10-day gap between the solar year (364 days) and the lunar year (354 days, that is, 12 × 29.5 = 354 synodic-month-days). The verse is preserved in the Aramaic 4Q209 fragment; the Aramaic preserves the calendrical-gap statement in fuller form than the Ge'ez. The 10-day gap is one of the central mathematical-problems of the Astronomical Book: the solar 364-day calendar (the calendrical-identity-keystone of the Qumran-Enochic-Jubilees corpus) and the lunar 354-day calendar (the proto-Rabbinic / Pharisaic Temple-Establishment framework) accumulate a 10-day-per-year discrepancy that the Astronomical Book preserves without an explicit harmonization-system. See central entry qumran-364-day-solar-calendar-polemic-1-enoch-72-82-jubilees-cross-corpus.

1 Enoch 75 — The four season-leaders and the epact-days that humans err in not counting

1
And the leaders of the heads of the days, whose rule is over the world together with the leaders over the seven stations of the sun — these their leaders encompass and supervise them.
And after that I saw thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand, I saw a multitude beyond number and reckoning, who stood before the Lord of Spirits. 2. And on the four sides of the Lord of Spirits I saw four presences, different from those that sleep not, and I learnt their names: for the angel that went with me made known to me their names, and showed me all the hidden things.
ወአዕራግ፡ wa-ʾaʿrāg ርእሰ፡ rəʾsa ዕለታት፡ ʿəlatāt መርሖሙ፡ marḥomu ዘበዐርብ፡ zaba-ʿarb መንግሥቶሙ፡ mangəśtomu ላዕለ፡ lāʿla ዓለም፡ ʿālam ላዕለ፡ lāʿla ስብዓቱ፡ səbʿātu መንበራት፡ manbarāt ለፀሐይ፡ la-ḍaḥay መርሖሙ፡ marḥomu ይትኬለልዎሙ፡ yətkēlaləwwomu ወያስተሣዕልዎሙ፡ wa-yāstaśāʿəlwommu
Notes Verse 1

The four season-leaders — the angelic supervisors of the four 91-day quarters. The Ge'ez ʾaʿrāg ('leaders / chiefs') introduces the four season-leaders who supervise the four 91-day quarters of the 364-day solar year. The four are named explicitly at 1 En 82:11-20 (Melkiel, Helemmelek, Meleyal, Narel — see commentary at ch 82). The angelic-administrative-leadership-of-the-seasons is integral to the 364-day-calendar framework. Uriel is the overall cosmic-administrative-angel; the four season-leaders are the next-level subordinates with portfolio over the four 91-day quarters. See central entries uriel-angel-over-luminaries-1-enoch-72-79-82-cross-corpus and qumran-364-day-solar-calendar-polemic-1-enoch-72-82-jubilees-cross-corpus.

2
And those four leaders of the east are surrounded by their leaders in their times; and Uriel, the holy angel who is their leader, said to me: their cause is the four days that are added, that are not counted in the reckoning of the year.
ወእልክቱ፡ wa-ʾəlləktu አርባዕቱ፡ ʾarbāʿtu ዘዐሥርቱ፡ zaʿaśərtu ምሥራቅ፡ məśrāq ይትኬለሉ፡ yətkēlalu መርሖሙ፡ marḥomu በበ፡ baba ጊዜሆሙ፡ gizēhomu ወይቤለኒ፡ wa-yəbēlanī ዑርኤል፡ ʿUrʾēl መልአክ፡ malʾak ዘውእቱ፡ zawəʾətu መርሖሙ፡ marḥomu ምክንያቶሙ፡ məkənyātomu አርባዕተ፡ ʾarbāʿta ዕለታት፡ ʿəlatāt ዘይትዌሰክ፡ zayətwēsak ኢተሐስቡ፡ ʾitaḥasabu በውስተ፡ ba-wəsta ኆለቅ፡ ḫolaq ለዓመት፡ la-ʿāmat
Notes Verse 2

The four epact-days polemic — stated in Uriel's own voice. This is one of the sharpest polemical-statements of the Astronomical Book. Uriel identifies the cause of the four 'leaders of the east' as the FOUR epact-days that are added (the days that bring the schematic 360-day base year to 364) — the days that 'are not counted in the reckoning of the year' by those who err in the calendar. The polemic targets the proto-Rabbinic / Pharisaic / Temple-Establishment tradition's lunar-solar calendar that does NOT count these four epact-days; the Astronomical Book holds the four epact-days as integral to the 364-day solar year. The polemic is sharpened at v. 3 ('humans err in these — they swiftly go astray concerning them') and continues at chs 82:4-6.

See central entry qumran-364-day-solar-calendar-polemic-1-enoch-72-82-jubilees-cross-corpus for the systematic treatment of the 364-day calendar as the calendrical-identity-keystone of the Qumran-Enochic-Jubilees corpus.

3
And humans err in these — they swiftly go astray concerning them — for those luminaries truly serve the seasons of the world in the stations of the world: one in the first gate, one in the third, one in the fourth, and one in the sixth.
And I heard the voices of those four presences as they uttered praises before the Lord of glory. 4. The first voice blesses the Lord of Spirits for ever and ever. 5. And the second voice I heard blessing the Elect One and the elect ones who hang upon the Lord of Spirits. 6. And the third voice I heard pray and intercede for those who dwell on the earth and supplicate in the name of the Lord of Spirits. 7. And I heard the fourth voice fending off the Satans and forbidding them to come before the Lord of Spirits to accuse them who dwell on the earth. 8. After that I asked the angel of peace who went with me, who showed me everything that is hidden: ‘Who are these four presences which I have seen and whose words I have heard and written down?’ 9. And he said to me: ‘This first is Michael, the merciful and long-suffering: and the second, who is set over all the diseases and all the wounds of the children of men, is Raphael: and the third, who is set over all the powers, is Gabriel: and the fourth, who is set over the repentance unto hope of those who inherit eternal life, is named Phanuel.’ 10. And these are the four angels of the Lord of Spirits and the four voices I heard in those days.

Notes Verse 3

'Humans err' — the sharpest polemical statement of the Astronomical Book. The Ge'ez wa-yətʿaḍāʿu ba-wəstētomu sabʾ wa-yəsaḥtu kiyāhu fəṭuna — 'humans err in these — they swiftly go astray concerning them' — names the calendrical-error directly as a human-error. The four epact-days are anchored in the four corner-gates of the sun's annual circuit: gate 1 (winter-solstice), gate 3 (vernal-equinox), gate 4 (summer-solstice), gate 6 (autumnal-equinox). The four 31-day-months at the solstice-and-equinox-junctures provide the four extra epact-days that the polemic targets.

The polemical-edge of v. 3 is one of the most-distinctive features of the Astronomical Book: the calendrical-difference is framed as a moral-error of humans, not merely a calculational-difference. The framework is shared with Jubilees 6:32-38 (the parallel polemic: 'they will forget the new moons and the times and the sabbaths, and they will make mistakes in all the new months and times and sabbaths').

Chapter 76

1 Enoch 76 — The twelve gates of the four winds at the ends of the earth

1
And at the ends of the earth I saw twelve gates open for all the winds, from which the winds come forth and blow upon the earth.
And after that I saw all the secrets of the heavens, and how the kingdom is divided, and how the actions of men are weighed in the balance. 2. And there I saw the mansions of the elect and the mansions of the holy, and mine eyes saw there all the sinners being driven from thence which deny the name of the Lord of Spirits, and being dragged off: and they could not abide because of the punishment which proceeds from the Lord of Spirits.
ובאפי u-ba-ʾappē ארעא ʾarʿāʾ חזית ḥăzēt עשרה ʿaśrāh ותרין u-tĕrēn תרעין tarʿīn פתיחין pětīḥīn לכל lě-kol רוחיא rūḥayyāʾ דמנהון dī נפקין minhōn רוחיא nāpĕqīn ונשבין rūḥayyāʾ על wě-nāšbīn ארעא ʿal
Notes Verse 1

The twelve gates and four winds cosmography — Aramaic-PRIMARY witness (4Q210 frag 1 col. ii). This verse opens 1 En 76's systematic cosmographic-meteorology framework: twelve gates of heaven (three at each of the four cardinal directions) through which the cosmic-winds blow. The framework is one of the most-elaborate cosmographic-systematizations of the Second-Temple-period apocalyptic-literature.

The framework extends the simpler 1 En 33-36 four-corners-and-gates cosmography (which has gates at the four cardinal-directions without the three-fold sub-division per direction) into a more-systematic 12-gate framework. The framework is paralleled in Zech 6:1-8 (the four chariots + four winds), Dan 7:2 (the four winds of heaven stirring the sea), Rev 7:1 (the four angels at the four corners holding back the four winds), and Sura 41:9-12 (the seven heavens + the cosmic-organization of the cosmos).

See central entry twelve-gates-four-winds-cosmography-1-enoch-76-cross-corpus.

2
Three of them are in the east of heaven, and three in the west, and three on the right of heaven, and three on the left.
תלתא tělātāʾ אנון ʾinnōn במדנח bě-madnāḥ שמיא šĕmayyāʾ ותלתא ū-tělātāʾ במערב bě-maʿărāb ותלתא ū-tělātāʾ בימינא bě-yāminā דשמיא dī-šĕmayyāʾ ותלתא ū-tělātāʾ בשמאלא bi-śĕmālāʾ
Notes Verse 2

Aramaic-PRIMARY witness — the 3+3+3+3 cardinal distribution. The Aramaic uses yamin / semal ('right / left' = south / north when oriented to the rising sun) — the standard Semitic cardinal-orientation convention where one orients the body to face east (the rising sun). The three-gates-per-cardinal-direction distribution (3 × 4 = 12 total) is the systematic framework that distinguishes 1 En 76 from the earlier four-corners cosmography of 1 En 33-36 (where each cardinal-direction has only one gate). Cross-corpus to Rev 21:13 (the New Jerusalem with three gates per cardinal direction: 3 × 4 = 12 gates total) — the Rev 21 framework directly parallels the 1 En 76 cosmographic systematization.

And there I saw closed chambers out of which the winds are divided, the chamber of the hail and winds, the chamber of the mist, and of the clouds, and the cloud thereof hovers over the earth from the beginning of the world. 5. And first the sun goes forth and traverses his path according to the commandment of the Lord of Spirits, and mighty is His name for ever and ever. 7. And after that I saw the hidden and the visible path of the moon, and she accomplishes the course of her path in that place by day and by night—the one holding a position opposite to the other before the Lord of Spirits. And they give thanks and praise and rest not; For unto them is their thanksgiving rest.

Chapter 77

1 Enoch 77 — The four quarters of the earth, the seven mountains, the seven rivers

1
And the first they call the east, because it is the first; and the second they call the south, because there the hand of every living thing is bowed down.
Wisdom found no place where she might dwell; Then a dwelling-place was assigned her in the heavens.
וקדמיתא u-qadmaytāʾ קרין qārēn לה lāh מדנחא madnāḥāʾ דהיא dī-hīʾ קדמיתא qadmaytāʾ ותניתא u-tinyāytāʾ קרין qārēn לה lāh ימינא yāminā דבה dī-bāh כפיף kāpēp ידא yědāʾ דכל dī-kol חי ḥay
2
And the third they call the west, because there all the lights of heaven are gathered in, and they set there toward the west; and the fourth they call the north, because in it are hidden all the works of the Cherubim and the Seraphim, and there is the dwelling-place of the Most High.
Wisdom went forth to make her dwelling among the children of men, And found no dwelling-place: Wisdom returned to her place, And took her seat among the angels.
ותליתיתא u-tělītāytāʾ קרין qārēn לה lāh מערבא maʿarbāʾ די dī תמן tammān עזלין ʿāzělīn כל kol נהורי něhōrē שמיא šěmayyāʾ ותתבון wě-yātbūn תמן tammān למערב lě-maʿărāb ורביעיתא u-rěbīʿāytāʾ קרין qārēn לה lāh צפונא ṣěpōnāʾ די dī-bāh בה mistattěrīn מסתתרין kol כל ʿōbědē עבדי kěrūbīm כרובים wě-śěrāpīm ושרפים u-bāh ובה miškěnāʾ משכנא dī-ʿillāʾāʾ דעליא
Notes Verse 2

THE NORTH AS DWELLING-PLACE OF THE MOST HIGH — Aramaic-PRIMARY witness (4Q210). This is one of the most-cosmographically-significant statements in the Astronomical Book: the cosmic-north is the dwelling-place of the Most High. The verse extends the broader Northwest-Semitic + Hebrew Bible north-as-cosmic-mountain tradition that runs through:

  • Ps 48:3 yarketê ṣāpôn qiryat melek rāḇ — Mount Zion 'in the recesses of the north' (the Hebrew tradition transferring Mount Ṣapunu's cosmic-mountain attributes onto Zion).
  • Isa 14:13 — the proud claim of the Day-Star-son-of-Dawn to ascend to 'the mount of assembly in the recesses of the north' (yarketê ṣāpôn).
  • Ezek 1:4 — the storm-wind from the north opening the throne-vision.
  • Ugaritic Mount Ṣapunu — Baʿlu's cosmic-mountain located geographically at Jebel al-Aqra ~50 km north of Ugarit.

The 1 En 77:2 statement makes the north-as-divine-dwelling explicit in the Second-Temple-Jewish apocalyptic-cosmographic register. The Cherubim and Seraphim — the angelic-throne-attendant orders (Ezek 1 + Isa 6) — are located in the cosmic-north as the throne-vision-tradition cosmographic-locale. See central entry north-as-dwelling-of-most-high-1-enoch-77-2-ps-48-2-zaphon-cross-corpus and the bidirectional-extension of mount-sapunu-tsafon-cosmic-mountain-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible.

3
And the regions of the earth are three: the first toward the east, and the second toward the south, and the third toward the west.
And unrighteousness went forth from her chambers: Whom she sought not she found, And dwelt with them, As rain in a desert And dew on a thirsty land.

And I saw seven great mountains, greater than all the mountains that are upon the earth; from them come forth snow, and the days and the seasons and the years pass by.

Notes Verse 4

The seven mountains — Aramaic-PRIMARY witness (4Q210). The seven-mountains cosmography here extends the seven-mountains cluster of 1 En 18:6-9 + 24:1-25:7 (the cosmic-mountains-of-precious-stones with the central seventh-mountain as the throne-of-glory site) into the broader cosmographic-treatise of ch 77. The seven-mountains framework is one of the most-systematic apocalyptic-cosmographic extensions of the Northwest-Semitic single-cosmic-mountain tradition (Mount Ṣapunu / Mount Zion / Mount Sinai) into the structured-seven-fold-enumeration register.

See central entry seven-mountains-of-god-1-enoch-18-24-cosmic-mountain-cluster-extension-cross-corpus (extended in this Editor pass to include ENO-WOH-77:4-5).

5
And I saw seven great rivers, greater than all the rivers — the first of them, the great one called Gihon; and the second, the Tigris; and the third, the Euphrates.
ושבעה u-šibʿāh נהרין nahărīn רברבין rabrěbīn חזית ḥăzēt מן min כל kol נהריא nahărayyāʾ קדמיא qadmāyāʾ מנהון minhōn רבא rabbāʾ דאקרי dī-ʾiqrē גיחון Gēḥōn ותנינא u-tinyānāʾ דקלת Diqlat ותליתיא u-tělītāyāʾ פרת Pěrāt
Notes Verse 5

The seven rivers — Aramaic-PRIMARY witness (4Q210); cross-corpus to Gen 2:10-14 Eden-rivers. The seven-rivers framework extends Gen 2:10-14's four Eden-rivers (Pishon, Gihon, Hiddekel/Tigris, Euphrates) into a structured-seven-fold-enumeration. The first three rivers — Gihon, Tigris, Euphrates — are three of the four Gen 2:10-14 Eden-rivers; the fourth Eden-river (Pishon) is absent in the 1 En 77:5 explicit enumeration but is likely among the remaining four rivers named at v. 6 (the Ge'ez of v. 6 has corrupted name-forms — possibly Harmon/Harahot and the Nile). The seven-rivers framework is the cosmographic-apocalyptic extension of the Eden-rivers tradition into the Astronomical-Book cosmographic register.

ወሰብዐ፡ wa-sabʿa አዕያት፡ ʾaʿyāt ዐበይተ፡ ʿabayta ርእኩ፡ rəʾku ዘመሐልዮ፡ zamaḥalyo ኮኑ፡ konu ሠለስቱ፡ śallastu መንገለ፡ mangala ምሥራቅ፡ məśrāq ወክልኤቱ፡ wa-kəlʾētu መንገለ፡ mangala ጾታ፡ ṣotā ወክልኤቱ፡ wa-kəlʾētu መንገለ፡ mangala ምዕራብ፡ məʿrāb
Chapter 78

1 Enoch 78 — The names of the sun and moon, and the lunar month

1
And the names of the sun are these: the first, Oryares; the second, Tomos.
And I saw other lightnings and the stars of heaven, and I saw how He called them all by their names and they hearkened unto Him. 2. And I saw how they are weighed in a righteous balance according to their proportions of light: (I saw) the width of their spaces and the day of their appearing, and how their revolution produces lightning: and (I saw) their revolution according to the number of the angels, and (how) they keep faith with each other. 3. And I asked the angel who went with me who showed me what was hidden: ‘What are these?’ 4. And he said to me: ‘The Lord of Spirits hath showed thee their parabolic meaning (lit. 'their parable'): these are the names of the holy who dwell on the earth and believe in the name of the Lord of Spirits for ever and ever.’
ወስማቲሆሙ፡ wa-səmātihomu ለፀሐይ፡ la-ḍaḥay እሉ፡ ʾəllu ቀዳማይ፡ qadāmāyə ኦርያረስ፡ ʾOryāras ካልዕ፡ kāləʿ ቶሞስ፡ Tomos
Notes Verse 1

The corrupted Ge'ez sun-names — preserved verbatim without emendation. The Ge'ez tradition has preserved sun-names ('Oryares', 'Tomos') in unrecognizable-corrupted forms that do not correspond to known Hebrew, Aramaic, or Greek astronomical-naming-systems. Multiple speculative reconstructions have been proposed: Charles 1912 conjectured Oryares < ʾōr-yāreaḥ ('light of the moon' — sun/moon-pair context corruption) and Tomos < Aramaic Tammūz (the Mesopotamian solar-deity-name); Neugebauer 1981 proposed Greek-loanword readings (ouranos + chōmos). None of the proposed reconstructions has achieved scholarly consensus.

The WoH translation preserves the corrupted Ge'ez forms verbatim without proposing emendations, per the overlay convention corrupted-geez-sun-moon-names-78-1-2-preserve-verbatim-no-emendation-convention. The corrupted-names are part of the source-text-historical-witness situation; emendation would require speculation about lost-original-forms that current scholarship does not warrant.

2
And the moon has four names: the first, Asanaya; the second, Abal; the third, Banase; the fourth, Erae.
ወወርኅሰ፡ wa-warḫəsa አርባዕቱ፡ ʾarbāʿtu ስማቲሁ፡ səmātihu ቀዳማይ፡ qadāmāyə አሰናያ፡ ʾAsanāyā ወካልዕ፡ wa-kāləʿ አበል፡ ʾAbal ወሣልስ፡ wa-śāləs በናሴ፡ Banāsē ወራብዕ፡ wa-rābəʿ ኤራዔ፡ ʾĒraʾē
Notes Verse 2

The corrupted Ge'ez moon-names — preserved verbatim without emendation. The Ge'ez moon-names (Asanaya, Abal, Banase, Erae) are similarly preserved in unrecognizable-corrupted forms. The four-fold structure likely corresponds to the four lunar phase-quarters (new-moon, first-quarter, full-moon, last-quarter) but the specific names do not correspond to known Hebrew or Aramaic lunar-phase vocabulary. The WoH translation preserves the corrupted Ge'ez forms verbatim per the overlay convention.

3

6
And on her first day her light becomes a measure — by seven parts, one of the sun's light becomes hers; and her light diminishes from what was of the first day: seven parts of seven.
ወበቀዳሚት፡ wa-ba-qadāmit ዕለታ፡ ʿəlatā ይከውን፡ yəkawwən ምዕር፡ məʿr ስብዐ፡ səbʿa ምክፋላት፡ məkfālāt ኮኖ፡ kono አሐደ፡ ʾaḥada ለብርሃኑ፡ la-bərhānu ለፀሐይ፡ la-ḍaḥay ወብርሃና፡ wa-bərhānā የሐጽጽ፡ yaḥaḍḍəḍ እምነ፡ ʾəmənna ዘኮነ፡ zakona በዘ፡ baza ቀዳሚት፡ qadāmit ዕለታ፡ ʿəlatā ስብዐ፡ səbʿa ምክፋላት፡ məkfālāt ስብዐ፡ səbʿa
Notes Verse 6

The 7×7 = 49-unit lunar-disk-fraction grid — Aramaic-fuller-than-Ge'ez. The verse fragmentarily preserves the seven-part-of-seven-parts (= 49-unit) lunar-disk-fraction framework that underlies the Astronomical Book's lunar tables. The Aramaic 4Q208 + 4Q209 DSS fragments preserve the full day-by-day 49-unit moonlight grid for the 14-day waxing + 14-day waning synodic cycle; the Ge'ez compresses to ~5× shorter summary statements. The witness-fullness inversion (Aramaic preserves more than Ge'ez) is one of the most-distinctive textual-features of the Astronomical Book. See overlay entry aramaic-fuller-than-geez-lunar-tables-4q208-convention and the foundational scholarly treatment in Drawnel 2011.

7

8
And there comes a time, a hidden place, a measure: seven parts together with all — for her first light, seven.
ወትከውን፡ wa-təkawwən ጊዜ፡ gizē መካን፡ makān ስቱረ፡ sətura ምዕር፡ məʿr ምክፋላት፡ məkfālāt ስብዐ፡ səbʿa ምስለ፡ məsla ኵሉ፡ kwəlu ለቀዳማይ፡ la-qadāmāyə ብርሃና፡ bərhānā ስብዐ፡ səbʿa

1 Enoch 79 — Uriel's closing summary of the astronomical revelation
